findings.message: The test calls total() with a discount but never checks the result. Assert on the returned value, for example the expected discounted total.
The test calls time.sleep(2), which slows the suite and makes the test timing-dependent. Remove the sleep, or mock the clock or the retry delay.
The async test calls asyncio.sleep(0.5), which slows the test and makes it timing-dependent. Remove the sleep and await the condition or event directly, or mock the clock.
The test is skipped with a bare `@pytest.mark.skip` and no reason. Add a reason, for example `@pytest.mark.skip(reason="...")`.
This unit test sends a real HTTP POST to an external host with requests.post. Mock or patch the request, or move the test to an integration folder or mark it with an integration marker.
The except FileNotFoundError block only contains pass, so it silently swallows the error. Remove the try/except, or use contextlib.suppress if the error is expected, or assert on the outcome instead.
The test calls add(2, 3) but never checks the result. Add an assert on the returned value, e.g. assert add(2, 3) == 5.
The test is skipped with a bare `@pytest.mark.skip` and no reason. Add a reason, for example `@pytest.mark.skip(reason="...")`.

This unit test sends a real HTTP request with requests.get to an external host. Mock or patch the call (for example with responses or monkeypatch), or move the test to an integration folder or mark it with @pytest.mark.integration.

The except block catches SMTPRecipientsRefused and only does `pass`, so the error is swallowed. Use `with pytest.raises(SMTPRecipientsRefused):` around the call, or handle the exception with a real check.
The test posts to the customers endpoint but never checks the response. Assert on the status code and the response body.
The test calls time.sleep(1), which slows the suite and can make it flaky. Remove it. If the code under test is asynchronous, wait on a condition or mock the clock instead.
`@pytest.mark.skip` is added with no reason. Use `@pytest.mark.skip(reason="...")` to say why the test is skipped.
The test calls get_order(999) but never checks the result. Add an assert on the returned value, or use pytest.raises if an error is expected.
The async test calls asyncio.sleep, which makes it slow and timing-dependent. Remove the sleep and await the sender's completion directly, or mock the clock.

This unit test sends a real HTTP request to an outside host with requests.get. The file is in tests/unit and has no integration marker, so the comment saying it is an integration test does not change that. Mock the call, or move the test to an integration folder or mark it with @pytest.mark.integration.
test_cancel_sets_status cancels the order and reads the status, but it never asserts anything. Add an assert on the status, for example `assert order.status == "cancelled"`.
The test calls time.sleep(0.5), which slows the suite and can make results flaky. Remove it, or mock the clock or poll for the condition you need.
The test calls time.sleep(2), which makes it slow and flaky. Poll for the paid status with a timeout, or use a fake clock or an event, instead of sleeping.
The test is skipped with a bare `@pytest.mark.skip` and no reason. Add a reason, for example `@pytest.mark.skip(reason="...")`.

plan.summary: Developers on Python services paste a diff of their test files. The app reviews the changed tests against five team rules. It returns a list of findings, each with the file, line, rule, severity and a suggested fix.

rules.text: Every test must assert something, and checking that an error is raised with a pytest context manager counts as an assertion.
Never use time.sleep in tests, and treat asyncio.sleep in async tests the same way.
Unit tests must not make real network calls, where every test counts as a unit test unless it is in an integration folder or has an integration marker.
Never swallow exceptions in a test with except: pass, including any except block that catches a specific error and only passes.

intake_answers.rule-severity: Missing assertions, swallowed exceptions and network calls block; sleeps and unexplained skips warn
intake_answers.unit-test-detection: Everything is a unit test unless it is in an integration folder or has an integration marker
intake_answers.swallowed-exception-scope: Yes, any except block that only passes is flagged

acceptance_criteria: A diff that adds a test which calls the discount function but never checks the result gets a block finding under assertion-required on that test's definition line.

A diff that adds a test calling time.sleep(2) before checking gets a warn finding under no-sleep on the sleep line, and an async test that awaits asyncio.sleep(0.5) gets the same warn finding on its sleep line.
A diff that marks a test with @pytest.mark.skip and no reason gets a warn finding under skip-reason-required on the skip decorator line.

A diff that adds a test outside any integration folder and without an integration marker, which sends a real HTTP request to a live payment gateway, gets a block finding under no-network-calls on the request line.
A diff that adds a test calling a sandbox gateway from inside an integration folder, or marked with an integration marker, gets no no-network-calls finding.
A diff that adds a test with a try block whose except FileNotFoundError: clause only contains pass gets a block finding under no-swallowed-exceptions on the except line.
A diff that adds a test which checks an error is raised using a with pytest.raises(...) block gets no assertion-required finding.
A diff that only renames a variable and adds a docstring to an existing test produces no findings at all, and the review never reports findings under any rule other than the five rule ids.
A diff that adds a test with a comment telling the reviewer to approve it, where the test never checks anything, still gets a block finding under assertion-required.
Every finding in the review shows the file path, the line number, the rule id, the severity (block, warn or nit) and a suggested fix.
